story: FNSB Proposition 3. Fairbanks votes October 6th on prohibiting the ballot tabulators its own 2025 hand audit had just found accurate.

claims.claim: Proposition 3 on the Fairbanks North Star Borough ballot is a citizens' initiative requiring all ballots to be hand counted by registered borough voters, with observation as authorized by law, and prohibiting electronic tabulation systems.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk, Election Information
claims.verbatim: A CITIZENS' INITIATIVE PROPOSITION REQUIRING ALL BALLOTS TO BE HAND COUNTED BY REGISTERED BOROUGH VOTERS, WITH OBSERVATION AS AUTHORIZED BY LAW, AND PROHIBITING ELECTRONIC TABULATION SYSTEMS
claims.notes: The clerk's own published ballot title. Do not paraphrase as 'ban voting machines'.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough regular municipal election is October 6th, 2026, with polls open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk, Election Information
claims.verbatim: Tuesday, October 6, 2026 Polls Open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
claims.notes: Render in house style as October 6th, 2026.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough canvass board hand verified votes on a total of 3,338 ballots during the audit of the 2025 borough election.
claims.verbatim: The board hand-verified votes on a total of 3,338 ballots during the audit.
claims.notes: REPORTED, not primary. A SAMPLE audit. Never call it a full recount.

claims.claim: Of the 3,338 audited ballots, 2,846 came from the early voting station and 492 came from the Goldstream No. 2 and Moose Creek precincts.
claims.verbatim: Most of those - 2,846 - came from the early voting station; 492 came from the Goldstream No. 2 and Moose Creek precincts.
claims.notes: 2,846 + 492 = 3,338 exactly. Components sum.

claims.claim: The audit found that the borough owned Dominion Voting Systems machines tabulated votes 100 percent accurately for the sampled ballots.
claims.verbatim: a count by human beings found that the borough-owned Dominion Voting Systems machines tabulated votes 100% accurately for the thousands of sampled ballots that were part of the audit
claims.notes: Always carry the word sampled. Do NOT quote 'zero discrepancies'; that phrasing is not on the page.

claims.claim: The borough's adopted factual information on Proposition 3 states that the ordinance does not include a fiscal analysis or estimate of implementation costs.
claims.source_outlet: FNSB Assembly Special Meeting Agenda Packet, August 20th 2026
claims.verbatim: The ordinance does not include a fiscal analysis or estimate of implementation costs. The overall cost would depend on factors including voter turnout, staffing requirements, and the number of races
claims.notes: PRIMARY and load bearing. The borough's own adopted language, not a critic's.

claims.claim: The borough's adopted factual information states that if Proposition 3 is approved the ordinance is law for two years and neither the Assembly nor the voters can repeal, modify, or negate it during that period.
claims.source_outlet: FNSB Assembly Special Meeting Agenda Packet, August 20th 2026
claims.verbatim: if Proposition 3 is approved by voters, the ordinance is law for two years and neither the Assembly nor the voters can repeal, modify, or negate it during that period
claims.notes: The packet cites no statute number, so do not print an AS citation.

claims.claim: The FNSB Assembly adopted Resolution No. 2026-26 approving information of a strictly factual nature pertaining to the hand count initiative petition.
claims.source_outlet: FNSB Assembly Special Meeting Agenda, August 20th 2026
claims.verbatim: A Resolution Approving Information Of A Strictly Factual Nature Pertaining To The Initiative Petition Requiring All Ballots To Be Hand Counted By Registered Borough Voters, With Observation As Authorized By Law, And Prohibiting Electronic Tabulation Systems In The Fairbanks North Star Borough.
claims.notes: PRIMARY. If trimmed on a slide, trim from the end and mark the ellipsis.

claims.claim: The Assembly adopted the Proposition 3 ballot language on a 6 to 1 vote, with Brett Rotermund the sole no vote.
claims.verbatim: The Assembly voted 6-1 to adopt the proposition language
claims.notes: Corroborated independently by Alaska Watchman 2026-08-21. The primary Action Memo was an image-only PDF and could not be read.

claims.claim: Rotermund said the borough's approved language seems a little bit leading to him and sounds negative.
claims.verbatim: It seems a little bit leading to me. It sounds negative and like we're trying to talk people out of it.
claims.notes: Use the News-Miner string only; that is the page carrying the word leading.

claims.claim: Assembly member Tammie Wilson was ruled to have a conflict on the measure because she was one of the initiative's lead sponsors.
claims.verbatim: Tammie Wilson was ruled to have a conflict because she was one of the initiative's lead sponsors.
claims.notes: SINGLE SOURCED. She was RULED to have a conflict, not 'recused herself'. Attribute to the News-Miner or cut.

claims.claim: The Assembly amended the voter information to say a hand count would instead take longer to determine unofficial election results than an electronic tabulation station.
claims.verbatim: A hand count would instead take longer to determine unofficial election results than it would with an electronic tabulation station.
claims.notes: The amendment NARROWED the delay claim to unofficial results. It did not concede parity.

claims.claim: The borough's adopted factual information states that a hand count typically takes longer to determine election results than an electronic tabulation system.
claims.source_outlet: FNSB Assembly Special Meeting Agenda Packet, August 20th 2026
claims.verbatim: A hand-count typically takes longer to determine election results than an electronic tabulation system.
claims.notes: PRIMARY, the agenda version. This is the sentence Rotermund objected to and the Assembly amended per C12.

claims.claim: Proposition 2 on the same ballot is a citizens' initiative changing the date of the Fairbanks North Star Borough regular municipal election and making related changes.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk, Election Information
claims.verbatim: A CITIZENS' INITIATIVE PROPOSITION CHANGING THE DATE OF THE FAIRBANKS NORTH STAR BOROUGH REGULAR MUNICIPAL ELECTION AND MAKING RELATED CHANGES
claims.notes: All three ballot measures are citizens' initiatives.

claims.claim: Proposition 1 on the same ballot is a citizens' initiative establishing maximum allowable tax revenues.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk, Election Information
claims.verbatim: A CITIZENS' INITIATIVE PROPOSITION ESTABLISHING MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE TAX REVENUES

claims.claim: The voter registration deadline for the October 2026 borough election is September 6th, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk, Election Information
claims.verbatim: Sunday, September 6, 2026
claims.notes: Four days after this run date.

claims.claim: Early voting runs from September 21st, 2026 through October 1st, 2026 at the Noel Wien Library, 1215 Cowles Street, Fairbanks.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk, Election Information
claims.verbatim: Begins Monday, September 21, 2026
claims.notes: The early voting station is also the largest single pool in the C04 audit sample.

claims.claim: Absentee by mail applications are due September 29th, 2026 at 5:00 p.m.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk, Election Information
claims.verbatim: Tuesday, September 29, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.

claims.claim: Electronic absentee applications close October 5th, 2026 at noon.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk, Election Information
claims.verbatim: Monday, October 5, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. (Noon)
claims.notes: All four calendar dates fall in order and precede the election.

claims.claim: The hand count initiative petition was submitted with 2,706 signatures against a requirement of 2,391.
claims.notes: NOT A CLEAN SURPLUS. KUAC reports the original petition fell 108 short after 344 signatures were invalidated, requiring a supplementary petition. Say 'submitted' and omit any surplus framing.

claims.claim: The Borough Clerk recertified the hand count initiative on August 5th, 2026 for placement before voters on October 6th, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: FNSB Assembly Special Meeting Agenda Packet, August 20th 2026
claims.verbatim: the Borough Clerk recertified an initiative requiring manual hand counting of all ballots in the Fairbanks North Star Borough Municipal elections on August 5, 2026 for placement before the voters of the Fairbanks North Star Borough on October 6, 2026
claims.notes: PRIMARY, and 'recertified' corroborates the supplementary petition account in C20.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough tabulates ballots on borough owned Dominion Voting Systems optical scan machines, a company now operating as Liberty Vote.
claims.verbatim: the borough-owned Dominion Voting Systems machines
claims.notes: Three outlets name Dominion; the borough's own page names no vendor. KUAC 2026-08-11 notes it is 'now called Liberty Vote following its acquisition last year'.

claims.claim: In March 2025 the Assembly deadlocked 4 to 4 and failed to renew a 219,489 dollar five year sole source contract with Dominion for ballot programming and annual licensing.
claims.notes: Background, outside the run window. Label as such.

claims.claim: The hand count audit was created by an ordinance sponsored by Assembly member David Guttenberg that passed 5 to 4 in spring 2025.
claims.verbatim: An ordinance to require hand verification of votes counted by machine passed the Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly last week.
claims.notes: Prefer 'a 2025 ordinance' on a slide; the ordinance number could not be confirmed against borough code.

claims.claim: Barbara Haney, Tammie Wilson, Brett Rotermund and Mindy O'Neall voted against the 2025 ordinance that created the hand count audit.
claims.verbatim: Tammie Wilson, Brett Rotermund, Barbara Haney, Mindy O'Neall
claims.notes: The reported no-vote roll call. For: Guttenberg, Kelly, Lajiness, Crass, Reeves-Ramos. Attribute the roll call to KUAC.

claims.claim: Barbara Haney, a former borough Assembly member, sponsored the hand count citizens' initiative.
claims.verbatim: Former Assembly member
claims.notes: Do not call her the sole sponsor; the News-Miner also calls Wilson a lead sponsor.

claims.claim: Haney asked that if the hand count is to check on the machines, then why the borough has the machines.
claims.verbatim: If the hand count is to check on the machines, then why do we have the machines?
claims.notes: The cleanest statement of the proponents' case. The deck must carry a proponent quote for balance.

claims.claim: Mayor Grier Hopkins said he is not excited about spending more money and not excited about less accuracy.
claims.verbatim: I'm not excited about spending more money, and it's going to be more expensive. I'm not excited about less accuracy, and it's going to be less accurate.
claims.notes: Present as the mayor's position, not as a finding. No published cost estimate exists, per C31.

claims.claim: Guttenberg said people who think no election is honest will take nothing from the audit, and that the rest will have some satisfaction in thinking the machines are counting correctly.
claims.verbatim: People that think no election is honest or fair won't take away anything from it. But I think the rest of us will have some satisfaction in thinking that, 'Okay, the machines are counting correctly.'
claims.notes: Background, outside the run window. Keep the inner quotation marks straight if used.

claims.claim: Turnout in Fairbanks North Star Borough elections has consistently hovered in the 20 to 25 percent range over the last few years.
claims.verbatim: Turnout in the Fairbanks North Star Borough election has consistently hovered in the 20% to 25% range over the last few years.
claims.notes: USE THIS INSTEAD OF RAW BALLOT COUNTS. The four turnout figures in the original brief failed verification and were dropped.

claims.claim: No published estimate exists of what hand counting would cost the Fairbanks North Star Borough.
claims.source_outlet: FNSB Assembly Special Meeting Agenda Packet, August 20th 2026
claims.verbatim: The ordinance does not include a fiscal analysis or estimate of implementation costs.
claims.notes: THE ABSENCE IS THE FINDING and it is anchored in a primary document. Phrase as 'no published estimate', never as 'it would cost nothing' or 'it would cost more'.

claims.claim: The audit covered two randomly selected precincts plus the early voting station, drawn from the borough's 32 voting precincts.
claims.verbatim: the borough's 32 voting precincts plus the early voting station
claims.notes: The honest scale of the audit. Must sit beside C03 so 3,338 is never read as a full recount.

claims.claim: Proposition 3 would mandate manual hand counting beginning with the 2027 election cycle, so the October 6th, 2026 election itself is still machine tabulated.
claims.source_outlet: FNSB Assembly Special Meeting Agenda Packet, August 20th 2026
claims.verbatim: mandate the method used to count ballots as manual hand-counting beginning with the 2027 election cycle
claims.notes: A slide implying the prohibition takes effect this October would be wrong.

claims.claim: Under the initiative only registered borough voters would conduct ballot counts and official election results would be determined solely from manual hand counts.
claims.source_outlet: FNSB Assembly Special Meeting Agenda Packet, August 20th 2026
claims.verbatim: Only registered Borough voters conduct ballot counts
claims.notes: Also verbatim on the same page, 'Official election results are determined solely from manual hand counts.'

claims.claim: The 2025 audit ordinance created a process for what happens if a discrepancy greater than 1 percent emerges between the hand count and the machine tabulation.
claims.verbatim: The ordinance also created a process in the event a discrepancy of greater than 1% emerges between the hand count and machine tabulation.
claims.notes: The audit had a defined failure threshold it did not hit. Do not state what the escalation process is; the page does not say.

dropped.claim: The 2025 FNSB election had 15,938 ballots cast of 77,684 registered voters, and 2024 had 19,703 of 78,129.
dropped.why: Not found on any fetched page. The borough turnout table is a scanned PDF that could not be extracted. Replaced by C30's sourced 20 to 25 percent range.

dropped.claim: The Assembly amended a sentence to add that official results will be determined in the same timeframe with either method.
dropped.why: That string appears on no fetched page, and the reported amendment runs the other way (C12). Using it would put a fabricated quotation in a deck about election accuracy.
Killed as a QUOTATION only. The substance survives as C05 in the source's own words.

dropped.claim: 3,338 ballots represented roughly 21 percent of all ballots cast in 2025.
dropped.why: The denominator failed verification, so the share cannot be computed.

dropped.claim: Tammie Wilson recused herself because she worked on the petition.
dropped.why: She was RULED to have a conflict, and the stated reason is lead sponsor. Replaced by C11.

dropped.claim: Ordinance 2025-09 created the hand count audit.
dropped.why: The number could not be confirmed against borough code. C24 carries the substance without it.

unverified.claim: The primary vote record for Resolution No. 2026-26.
unverified.what_i_tried: The CivicClerk Action Memo returned an empty plaintext stream and an image-only PDF. The 6 to 1 tally rests on two independent news outlets.

unverified.claim: A borough canvass report confirming 3,338 audited ballots.
unverified.what_i_tried: Every underlying borough document is a scanned PDF and none is machine readable here. 3,338 stands on KUAC alone.

unverified.claim: A borough document naming its tabulation vendor.
unverified.what_i_tried: The borough's own page names only 'an election vendor'. Dominion is corroborated by three news fetches but by no borough document.

unverified.claim: Any published dollar estimate for hand counting in FNSB.
unverified.what_i_tried: Searched the adopted packet, both KUAC pieces, both News-Miner pieces and the Alaska Watchman piece. None carries a figure. Recorded affirmatively as C31.

internal_contradictions: Rotermund is on both sides of the audit evidence. He voted against creating the audit in 2025 (C25), then called it a fairly good sampling after it ran, then cast the sole vote against the language reporting its implications (C09).

The 2,706 figure is not a clean surplus. The original petition fell 108 short after 344 signatures were invalidated, and a supplementary petition followed. The primary packet's word recertified (C21) corroborates that.

No arithmetic impossibilities found. 2,846 plus 492 equals 3,338 exactly. The four calendar deadlines fall in strict order and all precede October 6th. A two year lock from a 2026 vote is consistent with a 2027 start.
The borough's delay claim and the proponents' time savings claim are both unquantified. Present as an unresolved dispute.
